items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening prepositional phrase
items.stem: The orbit of several newly discovered planets ___ unusually stable.
items.answer_explanation: The singular head noun orbit requires the singular verb remains.

distractor_rationales.A: Remain agrees with the nearby plural noun planets, not the subject head.
distractor_rationales.C: The participle cannot serve as the finite predicate.
distractor_rationales.D: Has remain uses an incorrect participle form.

items.subtype: embedded question with noninverted word order
items.stem: Researchers are uncertain whether the pottery fragments ___ from the coastal settlement.
items.answer_explanation: An embedded whether-question uses statement word order: subject followed by the finite verb.

distractor_rationales.A: Inversion with did is not used in this embedded question.
distractor_rationales.B: The auxiliary is misplaced and the clause is ungrammatical.
distractor_rationales.D: This is not a complete finite clause.

items.subtype: restrictive relative pronoun as object
items.stem: The researcher cataloged the fern species ___ the expedition had collected.
items.answer_explanation: That correctly introduces a restrictive relative clause and functions as its object.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: that is the object of had collected.
distractor_rationales.B: What cannot follow an antecedent noun in this construction.
distractor_rationales.C: They creates an extra subject and leaves the object missing.
distractor_rationales.D: Which them contains a redundant object.

items.subtype: second conditional clause with full subordinate-clause structure
items.stem: If the city ___ the subsidy, more households would install efficient heating systems.
items.answer_explanation: The second conditional uses a simple past form in the if-clause and would plus base verb in the result.

distractor_rationales.A: The present tense does not form the intended second conditional.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: increased pairs with would install.
distractor_rationales.C: Will is not normally used in this if-clause.
distractor_rationales.D: The progressive form is not required and changes the construction.

items.subtype: concessive relation requiring a prepositional connector before a noun phrase
items.stem: ___ its low density, the alloy withstands considerable pressure.
items.answer_explanation: Despite is followed directly by a noun phrase and expresses concession.

distractor_rationales.A: Although requires a finite clause, not this noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.C: Despite of is not the standard prepositional form.
distractor_rationales.D: Because expresses cause rather than concession.

items.subtype: passive voice in a finite main clause
items.stem: The storm system ___ by satellite instruments before it reached the coast.
items.answer_explanation: The system receives the action, so the finite passive was tracked is required.

distractor_rationales.A: Was tracking gives the subject an agentive meaning.
distractor_rationales.B: Tracked is active and lacks an expressed agent.
distractor_rationales.D: Tracking is a nonfinite fragment here.

items.subtype: causative make followed by object and adjective complement
items.stem: The new park design made the narrow corridor ___ and safer for pedestrians.
items.answer_explanation: Make takes an object followed by a bare adjective complement; wider is coordinated with safer.

distractor_rationales.A: Make does not take a to-infinitive complement in this frame.
distractor_rationales.B: The participle is not parallel with safer.
distractor_rationales.C: Widened suggests a passive result and is not coordinated with safer.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: made the corridor wider and safer.

items.subtype: reduced passive relative clause with a past participle
items.stem: The fibers ___ with a protective coating retain their strength after repeated washing and drying.
items.answer_explanation: Treated is a reduced passive relative clause modifying fibers: fibers that were treated.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: treated means that were treated.
distractor_rationales.B: Treating gives the fibers an incorrect active role.
distractor_rationales.C: Were treated creates a second finite verb in the noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: Having treat has an incorrect participle form.

items.subtype: so plus adjective licensing a result that-clause
items.stem: The memory task was so demanding that several participants, after practicing for weeks, ___ unable to finish it.
items.answer_explanation: So demanding that introduces a result clause whose finite predicate is were unable.

distractor_rationales.A: More unable is an unnecessary and awkward degree form.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: participants were unable to finish.
distractor_rationales.C: Being is nonfinite and cannot complete the clause.
distractor_rationales.D: Had been to does not provide the required predicate.

items.subtype: not only but also with coordinated finite verbs
items.stem: The software not only records performances but also ___ background noise automatically.
items.answer_explanation: Not only records but also filters coordinates two finite verbs with the same subject.

distractor_rationales.A: Filtering is not parallel with the finite verb records.
distractor_rationales.B: The to-infinitive is not parallel with records.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: records and filters are coordinated finite verbs.
distractor_rationales.D: The past tense breaks the intended present-tense coordination.

items.subtype: appositive noun phrase in post-subject position
items.stem: Marie Curie, a pioneer in radioactivity research, ___ two Nobel Prizes.
items.answer_explanation: The appositive is parenthetical, so the sentence needs the finite verb received.

distractor_rationales.A: Awarding is nonfinite and lacks a main verb.
distractor_rationales.B: Was award has an incorrect passive form.
distractor_rationales.C: Her award is a noun phrase, not a predicate.

items.subtype: elliptical conditional inversion with had
items.stem: Had the reef restoration project ___ earlier, the damaged habitat might have recovered before winter.
items.answer_explanation: Had plus the past participle forms an inverted past-perfect conditional: had begun.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: had begun is the inverted form of if the project had begun.
distractor_rationales.C: The inverted clause does not take an extra subject it.
distractor_rationales.D: Been begin uses an incorrect participle.

items.subtype: there plus be with a plural postverbal noun phrase
items.stem: There ___ several blank areas on the early map of the northern coast.
items.answer_explanation: The plural postverbal noun phrase areas requires are in this existential construction.

distractor_rationales.A: Is is singular and does not agree with areas.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: there are several blank areas.
distractor_rationales.D: Has does not form the existential construction here.

items.subtype: quantifier compatible with an uncountable noun
items.stem: The recipe requires ___ additional information about the nutritional content of the grain.
items.answer_explanation: Information is uncountable, so some is the compatible quantifier.

distractor_rationales.B: Few also modifies countable plural nouns.
distractor_rationales.D: Several requires a countable plural noun.

items.subtype: adverb required to modify a finite verb
items.stem: The archivist explained that the fragile documents must be handled ___ during the transfer.
items.answer_explanation: Carefully is the adverb modifying handled.

distractor_rationales.A: Careful is an adjective, not the required adverb.
distractor_rationales.C: Care is a noun or verb and cannot modify handled here.

items.subtype: indefinite article before a consonant-initial noun
items.sentence: A architect measured the vaulted entrance before the renovation began.
items.answer_explanation: The consonant letter a is pronounced with an initial vowel sound, so the article must be an.

items.subtype: adjective required before a head noun
items.sentence: The region experienced a dramatically temperature shift during the afternoon.
items.answer_explanation: Dramatic is the adjective required to modify temperature; dramatically is an adverb.

items.subtype: simple past finite verb in a completed historical sequence
items.sentence: The clinic introduced the screening program after it identify the main risk factors.
items.answer_explanation: The completed past event requires the simple past identified.

items.subtype: parallel gerund complements in a coordinated list
items.sentence: The course emphasizes reading technical articles, analyzing evidence, and to present findings clearly.
items.answer_explanation: The three complements after emphasizes must use parallel gerund forms.

items.subtype: adjective object complement after find
items.sentence: The court found the new evidence convincing for the jury.
items.answer_explanation: In this frame, the adjective convincing takes to before the recipient of the persuasion.

items.subtype: present participle in a reduced active clause
items.sentence: The buses traveling along the old route, carrying commuters into the city each morning.
items.minimal_correction: The buses travel along the old route, carrying commuters into the city each morning.
items.answer_explanation: The sentence needs a finite main verb; traveling alone leaves the subject without a predicate.

items.subtype: although introducing a finite concessive clause
items.sentence: Despite the market was unstable, investors continued to purchase municipal bonds.
items.answer_explanation: A finite clause requires although, whereas despite must be followed by a noun phrase or gerund.

items.subtype: relative pronoun as the object of a preposition
items.sentence: The plant is one of the species with whom the botanist has worked for years.

marked_parts.D: the botanist has worked for years

items.answer_explanation: Which refers to the plant species; whom is used for people.

items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening modifier
items.sentence: The pattern of clouds over the mountain indicate an approaching storm.
items.answer_explanation: The singular head noun pattern requires indicates.

items.subtype: quantifier compatible with a countable plural noun
items.sentence: Only much of the dietary samples contained enough iron for the analysis.
items.answer_explanation: Samples is a countable plural noun, so many, not much, is required.

items.subtype: noun required as the head of a prepositional object
items.sentence: The lecturer discussed the historical develop of the regional dialect.
items.answer_explanation: The premodifier historical requires the noun development as the head of the phrase.

items.subtype: passive participle after a finite form of be
items.sentence: The components were assembling in a sealed chamber to prevent contamination.
items.answer_explanation: The components receive the action, so be must be followed by the passive participle assembled.

items.subtype: parallel noun phrases after not only but also
items.sentence: The proposal addresses not only traffic congestion but also should improve pedestrian safety.
items.answer_explanation: The two objects of addresses must be parallel noun phrases: traffic congestion and pedestrian safety.

items.subtype: gerund as the complement of a preposition
items.sentence: The analyst succeeded in predict the quarterly trend despite limited data.
items.answer_explanation: The preposition in takes a gerund complement, predicting.

items.subtype: comparative adjective required by than
items.sentence: The eastern plateau is high than the valley during the dry season.
items.answer_explanation: Than requires the comparative form higher.

items.subtype: adjective order inside a noun phrase
items.sentence: The museum displayed a clay ancient vessel from the excavation.
items.minimal_correction: an ancient clay vessel from the excavation
items.answer_explanation: The age adjective precedes the material adjective: an ancient clay vessel.

items.subtype: singular pronoun agreement with an indefinite antecedent
items.sentence: Each storyteller adapted their account to suit the audience.
items.answer_explanation: In the locked traditional agreement pattern, singular each requires a singular pronoun.

items.subtype: predicate adjective after a linking verb
items.sentence: The amendment appears in constitutional after the court's review.
items.answer_explanation: Appear takes the predicate adjective directly; the inserted preposition in is not part of the linking-verb frame.

items.subtype: adverb required to modify a research verb
items.sentence: The librarian organized the archived manuscripts methodical.
items.answer_explanation: The verb organized is modified by the adverb methodically, not the adjective methodical.

items.subtype: infinitive of purpose after a finite verb
items.sentence: The volunteers collected water samples monitor pollution levels in the wetland.
items.answer_explanation: The infinitive marker to is required before the purpose verb monitor.

items.subtype: fixed preposition collocation after benefit
items.sentence: The observatory benefits from clear skies and benefits to precise measurements.
items.answer_explanation: Benefit takes the preposition from when it means to gain an advantage from something.

items.subtype: parallel finite verbs in a coordinated predicate
items.sentence: The conductor rehearsed the ensemble and checking the balance of the brass section.

marked_parts.D: the balance of the brass section

items.answer_explanation: Rehearsed and checked are coordinated finite past-tense verbs with the same subject.

items.subtype: singular agreement after each
items.sentence: Each of the historic vehicles require careful maintenance.
items.answer_explanation: The subject each is singular, so the verb must be requires.

items.subtype: past perfect for the earlier of two past events
items.sentence: The geologists realized that the glacier melted before they had reached the valley.
items.answer_explanation: The earlier melting event takes the past perfect had melted relative to the later realization.

items.subtype: postpositive adjective phrase following an indefinite pronoun
items.sentence: The treatment plant needs something useful for removing sediment efficiently.
items.minimal_correction: needs something to remove sediment efficiently
items.answer_explanation: The adjective useful does not express the intended function; the unique grammatical repair is the purpose infinitive to remove.
